MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 5, 2020

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its meeting on
Wednesday, August 5, 2020 in the Council Chambers on the ninth
floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of Allegiance by
Commissioner Trejo, the meeting was called to order at 7:10 p.m.,
to allow the listening and watching audience an opportunity to
dial in.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated first:
   Staff has a newly revised meeting agenda with changes to the
  first paragraph with new Date and new Access Code for the
  Public to use for calling into the planning commission
  meeting.
   Staff has a new staff report and resolution with minor
  revisions to be addressed by staff, Mr. Salazar at the time
  of his presentation.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Chairman Springs opened the phone lines through AT&T On-Line
System.

There were none, and this was confirmed by the AT&T Operator.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-004 (SP-2020-004) 3900 WEST CENTURY
BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application by Shomof
Hospitality, LLC, for Special Use Permit No. 2020-004 (SP-2020-
004) to allow 1) the on-site consumption of beer and wine and
distilled spirits, 2) outdoor dining, and 3) outdoor live
entertainment within a hotel, hotel restaurant, and hotel pool
lounge on an approximately 86,102 square-foot, M-1L (Limited
Manufacturing) zoned property at 3900 West Century Boulevard.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the staff presentation.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020
Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff several questions –
 There are two areas that staff is speaking about the square
  footage of the property, one being utilized for live
  entertainment and a disk jockey and that would be 20 square
  feet?
  - Mr. Salazar replied that is correct, 20 square feet.
 And the next area is for 158 square footage area for an open
  air lounge area?
  - Mr. Salazar stated it is for the outdoor pool lounge and bar
  area.
 The west side of the building will be actually constructed on
  the property line, is that correct?
  - Mr. Salazar stated Yes, that is correct.
 In the event that there are guests entertaining on the second
  and third floors of the building, how does the Fire Department
  make entrance if there is an emergency?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the live entertainment is on the first
  floor. The Restaurants are on the first, second and on the
  roof deck and the Fire Department will have access through
  the front main entrance lobby. He stated there is also an
  entrance off Century Boulevard which will allow the Fire
  Department to enter the Hotel on the East Side of the building
  which will allow them to utilize the exterior of the building
  to the pool area.
 On the West side of the Building since this is being built on
  the property line, will there be a restriction of any other
  buildings or construction west of the building to that property
  line?
   Mr. Salazar stated that subject to the Inglewood Municipal
  Code, setbacks are not required for commercial property.

Commissioner Patrick stated:
 For clarification – there will be three restaurants in the
  hotel?
   Mr. Salazar stated that there is only one restaurant in the
  hotel, but it is three floors.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
• The pool-lounge building, is it open or enclosed?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the building is enclosed, however, it
  does have a roof-deck on top of the pool house area.
 Is this where the Live Entertainment will be?
   Mr. Salazar stated no, the Live Entertainment will take place
  on the east-side of the building and the Pool-lounge area.
 With regards to the pool-lounge area, is it open, enclosed with
  the pool included?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the pool along with the pool-lounge
  area is open from the roof-top grounds and up into the air.
 Are drinks served in the pool-lounge and pool areas?
   Mr. Salazar stated that there is a condition in the resolution
  that states there will be no alcohol served on the roof-top
  and in the pool lounge areas.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020

  Is there the possibility for a patron at the hotel who purchases
  alcohol at the bar area, and takes their drink over to the pool
  area, is there some way to insure that this does not occur?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the Planning Commission can amend the
  condition to prohibit the applicant from having alcohol
  served in the pool area and on the roof-top.
  She stated she feels this is the possible intent as guests would
  on their own, take their drinks to the pool and pool-lounge
  area.
  The last question is regarding the pool grounds area – (on page
  six, third paragraph from the bottom of the staff report) it
  states “live entertainment is intended for enjoyment of hotel
  guests and not for special events that bring non-hotel guests
  to the site”.
   Mr. Salazar stated that is correct. The municipal code states
  that businesses may have special events up to 4 times a year,
  without a special use permit, therefore it is by-right for 4
  times a year, going through the permits and licensing
  committee.
  Condition No. 8 reads: “An event center or private events at
  the hotel more than 4 times per year is subject to approval of
  a Special Use Permit.”
   Mr. Salazar stated - If the hotel wants to have the live
  entertainment more than 4 times per year, they would have to
  come before the Planning Commission to obtain a Special Use
  Permit to host an Event Center. Then if they are approved by
  the Planning Commission, they can host multiple events at the
  hotel.
  So if the hotel receives the permit, then non-hotel guests can
  enjoy the live entertainment? What is a special events and who
  would be responsible for enforcing it?
   Mr. Salazar stated a special event is typically Birthday
  Parties, Weddings, Family Reunions, those sorts of events.
  What about people who come into town not knowing about the
  special event requirements and their sole purpose of meeting
  together is to have a special family gathering say “ten
  families” get together event, and go over to the live
  entertainment area, it seems contradictory.
   Ms. Wilcox stated that typically another factor in obtaining
  a special event, it is held in a special area or is on the
  roof, is not opened to the general public and/or is closed
  off to other Hotel Guests. If a group of Hotel guests were
  coming together for a dinner or in the pool area, that
  wouldn’t be considered a special event.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff -
• With regards to non-hotel guests attending a special event or
  coming to listen and enjoy the live entertainment, how will
  there be a distinction between hotel guests and non-hotel
  guests?
   Mr. Salazar stated that question can be answered by the
  applicant.
 Will there be a limit on the number of drinks served at the bars
  to the guests of the Hotel?
   Mr. Salazar stated again, that question can be answered by
  the applicant.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020
Chairman Springs asked staff;
 Presently the Hotel does not have a permit to run the hotel?
  But they are here tonight for us to give them a permit to sell
  beer, wine and distilled spirits, but they do not have a business
  license?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the hotel does not presently have an
  active business license as to date.
   Mr. Salazar said that typically the business license is
  obtained once the applicant receives a certificate of
  occupancy, once the project is complete.
 Final question is regarding the hotel obtaining a special use
  permit for having liquor within the bedrooms, and what is to
  stop the hotel guests from taking the liquor from their rooms
  to the pool lounge area?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the Municipal Code does not restrict
  hotel guests from bringing alcohol to the pool lounge area,
  but the hotel can monitor the guests to restrict the removal
  of alcohol from the rooms, the applicant is here and they can
  speak further about operations.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
the planning commission.

Ms. Tari Kuvhenguhwa, representative for the applicant and Mr.
Jimmy Shomof of Shomof Hospitality, LLC., addressed the planning
commission.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for the planning
commissioner’s questions via-phone-line to the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant;
• About the parking spaces and the location of the parking spaces
  and to please explain the driveways, where will they be on the
  property? Also, how does one enter and exit the hotel?
   Mr. Jimmy Shomof stated that there are an initial 20 spaces
  in the front of the Hotel and that is where the circular
  driveway is located, and that there are more parking spaces
  in the rear of the hotel, where it includes the two-way
  driveway around the entire hotel, and it leads to the rear of
  the hotel area. There will be parking spaces on either side
  of the hotel also.
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated that the entrance and exit to the hotel
  will be only in the front of the hotel on Century Boulevard,
  and traffic will enter from the east-bound traffic.

Commissioner Rice asked;
 The bar is not exclusively for the hotel guests, is it an open
  bar to the general public?
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated that is correct, like a regular
  restaurant and bar.
 He stated his concern is that the bar would be serving someone
  from the street who is not a hotel guest until closing time for
  the bar as late as 2:00am, and then there will be a heavily
  intoxicated individual loose on the street.
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated that ABC will require the hotel to
  have a last call for drinks as early as 12:00am, along with
  the hotel staff who will make sure that no one leaves the
  hotel under their own power intoxicated. There will also be
  security staff to ensure that the guests will not be allowed
  to leave the premises intoxicated.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020

  With regards to the last call cutoff time, he did not see that
  ABC would be determining the time, but would require the
  establishment to have a decent time set in place, and not 30
  minutes prior to closing.
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated that the decision to have the cutoff
  time in accord with the local establishments in the area,
  with the Hotel’s serving the majority of their alcohol with
  meals, as opposed to just having individuals sitting and
  drinking solely at the bar, they feel that this will be in
  line with ABC’s Hotel standards.

Commissioner Trejo asked;
 About the 98 parking spaces on the property, and will staff be
  utilizing some of the parking spaces as well as the hotel guests
  or not? And if not, where will Hotel staff be parking their
  vehicles all day?
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated that although it will be for both hotel
  guests and staff, it will also accommodate the restaurant
  guests and with different modes of transportation for people
  today such as Lyft, Uber, MTA, etc., along with the earlier
  mention of the grandfathered-in parking requirements, the
  hotel is more than within the requirements regarding parking
  provided spaces for the Hotel.
 Another issue is the “No drinks allowed in the pool lounge
  area”, that was the initial intent for the area, correct?
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated - The way the conditions read, looking
  at condition number 10, it has to deal with the roof top more
  so than the pool-lounge area and our request is that there be
  the allowance where if a patron is served at the pool-lounge
  area alcohol or food, that they will be allowed to take their
  drink with them, although staff will not do re-fills on the
  roof, but just to allow the hotel patrons to take their drinks
  with them wherever they wish to travel within the Hotel.
 Next question, if there is no security on site, how would the
  Hotel handle an unruly guest? How would that be dealt with?
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated that there will be security on site as
  condition number 14 requires two-armed security personnel on
  site at all times.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated -
 Looking at what the applicant stated that there will be only 20
  security cameras on the site, 8 of which will be at the rear of
  the hotel and in the parking lot and will there be foot patrol
  in the parking lot area?
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated yes there will be foot patrol in the
  parking lot area and around and inside the entire hotel along
  with staff from the hotel, all day and evening.
 How many cameras will be in the parking lot area alone?
   Ms. Kuvhenguhwa stated she would have to look on the plans to
  accurately state how many would be in the parking area.
   Mr. Shomof stated that he has increased the number of cameras
  on the premises, with ten cameras in the parking lot area and
  pointing to the rear and sides of the building, along with
  eight cameras in the front of the hotel and an additional 35-
  40 security cameras inside of the hotel to cover all floors.
   Mr. Salazar stated that the planning commission can condition
  for more security cameras if the Planning Commission feels
  that the applicant will need more, as part of the approval
  for this applicant.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020

  Just to clarify, Mr. Shomof are you stating that you have now
  increased your security cameras to a total of 40 cameras on the
  site?
   Mr. Shomof stated yes, that is correct. I just spoke to my
  architect today to increase the number of security cameras on
  the site and it comes to between 35 to 40.

Chairman Springs opened up the phone line for the public comments
to speak for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None. This was affirmed by the AT&T On-line Operator.

Chairman Springs asked for closing comments from the planning
commission regarding this item.

Commissioner Trejo stated -
 Just wanted to get clarification that on condition number 10,
  that hotel staff will not serve any beverages or food to hotel
  guests/patrons on the roof top, and that patrons are not allowed
  to bring with them their purchased drinks and food to the roof
  top?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the planning commission can make it
  a condition that there will be no food or drinks removed from
  the restaurant and pool-lounge area and taken to the roof top
  by patrons or staff.

Chairman Springs closed and thanked the Planning Commission for
their input, and asked for a motion regarding Special use Permit
No. 2020-004 (SP-2020-004).

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-032 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2020-004 with the 22 conditions as follows: 1) On-
site consumption of beer, wine and distilled spirits from a hotel
and hotel restaurant; 2) Outdoor Dining from a restaurant, roof
deck and a hotel pool lounge; 3) Outdoor Live Entertainment within
a hotel pool lounge; last want to require a one-year review of the
applicants license and Hotel since this is new territory and was
seconded by Commissioner Patrick, Resolution No. 1877;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR
  SHOMOF HOSPITALITY, LLC TO ALLOW 1) THE ON-
  SITE CONSUMPTION OF BEER, WINE AND DISTILLED
  SPIRITS, 2) OUTDOOR DINING, AND 3) LIVE
  ENTERTAINMENT  WITHIN  A  HOTEL,  HOTEL
  RESTAURANT, AND HOTEL POOL LOUNGE ON AN
  APPROXIMATELY  86,102  SQUARE-FOOT,  M-1L
  (LIMITED  MANUFACTURING)  ZONED  PROPERTY
  LOCATED AT 3900 WEST CENTURY BOULEVARD

Be approved.

Chairman Springs asked for questions from the planning commission.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-005 (SP-2020-005) AT 334 EAST
STEPNEY STREET.
A public hearing to consider an application by Patrick Purnag,
Owner, for Special Use Permit No. 2020-005 (SP-2020-005) to
subdivide a property into four (4) condominium units on an
approximately 7,500 334 East Stepney Street.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 How will the parking of one vehicle on Stepney Street work, how
  will that requirement work with it being on the public street?
   Mr. McCrumby stated per the TOD developments can count
  adjacent street parking towards meeting the parking
  requirement.
 How can you grant and secure a designated public parking space
  for a residential home, when that street is a main thoroughfare
  for the community, its open street parking? Does this mean that
  you will mark the street that this parking space is for this
  designated building?
   Ms. Wilcox stated the parking spot would not be designated
  specifically to the unit. The TOD plan allows that when there
  is unrestricted parking along the frontage of the property,
  you can count a limited number of street parking spaces
  towards meeting the parking requirements.
 It’s a possibility that the curb space may not be there. Thank
  you.
   Ms. Wilcox stated correct.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 No, my question was just answered regarding the street parking
  scenario.

Chairman Springs stated he had questions for staff –
 This is a special Use Permit to subdivide a property into four
  condominium units, is that correct?
   Mr. McCrumby stated yes, that is correct.
 Project Description page. the applicant requesting SUP approval
  to demolish all structures on the site and construct two
  detached two-story structures that will contain two, three-
  bedroom units.
   Mr. McCrumby, so within both structures will be two attached
  units each.
 Then on the next page of the staff report, the applicant is
  requesting the SUP approval of the development of three two-
  story residential condominium units? This sounds like a
  contradiction in requests, or was this miss-read?
   Mr. McCrumby stated that it must have been a typo that the
  request is for a total of four units, not three.

Commissioner Rice asks:
 When the applicant returns for their Site Plan Review, will it
  be before the Planning Commission or will it strictly be handled
  by staff internally?

  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020

   Mr. McCrumby stated it would be ministerial with staff. But
  it will also be sent to our architectural consultant.

Chairman Springs opened the floor and asked the applicant to come
forward and speak to the planning commission and tell how this
project will better serve the community.

   Mr. Patrik Purnag explained his project and how it will
  beautify the community and enhance the neighborhood.

Chairman Springs closed the floor for the planning commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 Her concern about the days of the week when construction
  operations along with times and hours during the day that will
  affect the neighbors and will there be a way for them to reach
  out to the applicant if there are any concerns of issues that
  that they need to address with you during the building of this
  project?
   Mr. Purnag stated yes, most assuredly. He stated that both
  neighbors on the left and right of his project have his
  personal cellphone number and he will definitely post signs
  for people in the neighborhood who need to reach him with any
  questions, can do so.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for public comments to speak for
or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST
None. This was affirmed by the AT&T On-line Operator.

Chairman Springs closed the floor for public comments to speak for
or against this project and asked for final comments from the
Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs called for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Patrick to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-014, and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2020-005 subject to 16 conditions and was seconded by
Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution No. 1878;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO
  PATRIK PURNAG, TO ALLOW THE DEVELOPMENT OF
  FOUR (4), TWO-STORY RESIDENTIAL CONDOMINIUM
  UNITS ON AN APPROXIMATELY 7,500 SQUARE-FOOT,
  R-3  (MULTIPLE-FAMILY  RESIDNTIAL)  ZONED
  PROPERTY AT 334 EAST STEPNEY STREET.

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

  8
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020
5C. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-007 (SP-2020-007) AT 837 SOUTH
PRAIRIE AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Jeff Williams,
representing 7-Eleven, for a Special Use Permit No. 2020-007 (SP-
2020-007) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site
consumption from a proposed convenience market on an approximately
9,083 square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 837
South Prairie Avenue.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asks staff:
 There is a large lot behind the laundromat in the rear, do you
  know if it is owned by the same property owner who is purchasing
  the 7-Eleven property?
   Ms. Fewell stated that it is not.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 What is the beer and wine floor area in the existing store
  compared to the proposed floor area for the new store?
   Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant will be able to answer
  that question.

Chairman Springs asked staff:
 The applicant has an existing state of California Department of
  Alcohol and Beverage license, where is the old location as
  opposed to the new location?
   Ms. Fewell stated that it is presently across the street at
  the south-west corner of Arbor Vitae and Prairie Avenue and
  the new location is across the street on the north-west side
  of Arbor Vitae and Prairie Avenue, where they will become a
  single tenant business.
 Will they take their business license with them?
   Ms. Fewell stated yes they will.

Chairman Springs asked for the applicant to come forward to speak
to the planning commission and address the reason why this project
should be approved.

Mr. Jeff Williams, 7-Eleven regional representative for the Los
Angeles / Inglewood area, spoke to the planning commission.

Mr. Jeffrey Powell, 7-Eleven field operations representative for
the Inglewood area stores, also spoke to the planning commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commissioners
to question the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant:
 What are their plans for staff parking and where will they park
  at the new location? What about the entering and exiting of
  vehicles at the new site, how many parking spaces will you have
  on your new site and will there be parking for store staff?
   Mr. Williams stated that they will acquire 14 parking spaces
  at the new site, where generally 7-Eleven only receives about
  6 parking spaces. Everything will remain the same with regards
  to the ingress and egress.
 How many 7-Elevens are there currently in the City of Inglewood?
   Mr. Williams stated that there are 11.

  9
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020

Commissioner Rice stated to the applicant:
 That he read all of the letters of support, he also read the
  letter of concern from the local residents in the area of the
  current 7-Eleven.
 He visited the current location and looked at the report of how
  there is a plan to do several modifications with regards to the
  installation of the new beverage bar and how there will be more
  space in the new location, yet his only concern is that once
  and if 7-Eleven is approved for this relocation, anyone can come
  into the City and by-right within the first six months, not have
  to come before the Planning Commission for a hearing of approval
  and apply and receive their own business license including a
  beer and wine license – thus creating a large saturation in the
  area.

Chairman Springs asked staff:
 Isn’t it true that the applicant is taking with him to the new
  location his beer and wine license?
   Ms. Wilcox stated that yes, it is true but by right and the
  City’s code, within six months anyone can open a similar type
  business along with receive a beer and wine license and not
  have to come before the planning commission.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant:
 Are the coolers typically locked at all of the 7-Eleven Stores?
   Mr. Williams stated that all of the new stores will have a
  new locking mechanism on the coolers, which is what will now
  be implemented, but previous older store locations do not
  have that type of mechanism, although they can be manually
  locked.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the public to speak For or
Against this project.

FOR / AGAINST
 Delia, Resident of Inglewood – Agree with new improvements to
  the 7-Eleven store and understands their desire for the
  improvements, but is not in favor of the closure of the
  Laundromat at the new location. She stated there is a new 7-
  Eleven on Arbor Vitae at the corner of Inglewood Avenue (which
  removed a Laundromat from that location), and forced the
  residents to go to the Laundromat on Prairie Avenue and Arbor
  Vitae, which is now closed for another 7-Eleven store, leaving
  one more Laundromat over a mile away, on the corner of Oak
  Street and Manchester Boulevard – which has completely
  inconvenienced the community as a whole.

Chairman Springs closed the floor and asked for further questions
and/or concerns from the Planning Commission.

There were no further comments from the community at this time,
per the AT&T Operator.

Commissioner Patrick had one final question for the applicant:
 Do you intend to have both stores operating at the same time,
  and how long do you think it would take you to close the older
  store and open the new store?
   Mr. Williams stated that both stores will not be operating
  simultaneously, first they will build the new location, and
  once it is ready for occupancy (if the project is approved by

  10
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 5, 2020
  the Planning Commission), then the old store will be closed
  and the new store will open for business.

Commissioner Rice asked staff a question:
 Stated that he has heard about in the past how the beer and wine
  coolers can be locked with a key which is kept at the front
  counter with the store staff, is this a condition and if yes,
  where in the staff report is mentioned?
   Ms. Fewell stated that it is mentioned and is condition no.
  13.

Chairman Springs had a question and statement for the applicant:
 With regards to the south-west corner at the old location and
  the north-west corner for the new location, will 7-Eleven be
  purchasers of the new location and/or just leasing of both
  properties?
   Mr. Williams stated that they do lease in the South-west
  present location and will continue to lease in the new
  location.
 In stating that if the applicant will be leasing the new
  location, just like they are leasing the old location, it
  appears that the applicant could have attempted to modify the
  previous location in an attempt to not disadvantage the
  surrounding community by forcing out the Laundromat which is a
  necessity to the community at large. There is a need in the
  community for that type of business, if the applicant has the
  funds to continue to lease more properties, why not stay in the
  present location and improve where they presently are, instead
  of inconveniencing the community.

Chairman Springs asked for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-044, stating that the determination was made
